title: Finite-stage descent from an algebraic normalized solution
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose that $B\cong U_{\mathfrak p}$ as $A$-algebras for a finitely generated $A$-algebra $U$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and a prime $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $P/K$ be algebraic, let $R_P$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $P$, and let $C_P$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_KP)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Assume additionally that $C_P$ is a finitely generated module over $B\otimes_AR_P$ via the canonical multiplication map [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Assume $R_P$ and $C_P$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], have finitely many maximal ideals, and for every maximal ideal $q$ of $C_P$ the contraction $n=q\cap R_P$ is maximal, the localizations $(R_P)_n$ and $(C_P)_q$ are discrete valuation rings, $n(C_P)_q=q(C_P)_q$, and $\kappa(q)/\kappa(n)$ is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] and finitely generated as a field extension. Then some finite subextension $K_0/K$ inside $P$ has the following property: writing $R_0$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $K_0$ and $C_0$ for the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_KK_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$, for every maximal ideal $q_0$ of $C_0$, $n_0=q_0\cap R_0$ is maximal, $(R_0)_{n_0}$ and $(C_0)_{q_0}$ are discrete valuation rings, $n_0(C_0)_{q_0}=q_0(C_0)_{q_0}$, and $\kappa(q_0)/\kappa(n_0)$ is separable. Here local means pulling back the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal, finite means finite-dimensional, and reduction means quotienting by all nilpotents. The given algebraic extension $P$ and its local properties are hypotheses, not an asserted existence conclusion.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, last three proof paragraphs: filtered union of finite K_i, stabilization of branches and uniformizers, and descent of separable residue equations.

proof.text: Index the finite subextensions $F/K$ inside $P$ by inclusion; this is a directed set (use the compositum of two finite extensions). Write $R_F,C_F$ for the normalizations in the statement. Both systems have injective integral transition maps, and $R_P=\bigcup_FR_F$, $C_P=\bigcup_FC_F$. Indeed an element of a tensor algebra is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a monic equation has finitely many coefficients, so an integral element and its equation occur at one finite stage. An equality modulo nilpotents is witnessed by one finite power and therefore also occurs at a finite stage. Extension of fields reflects nilpotence, so the maps of the reduced tensor algebras are injective. Each element of a later normalization is still integral over $A$ or $B$, hence over the earlier normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (a), to every finite $F/K$; apply case (b) to $P/K$, using the given essentially finite type presentation of $B$ and Noetherianity of $R_P$. Thus all normalizations have finitely many maximal ideals, maximal contractions, and the displayed local DVRs; in particular their sets of maximal ideals are finite and nonempty. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-algebraic-model], using exactly the extra finite-module hypothesis in the corrected statement. Start at its finite field $F_*$ and retain the canonical isomorphism $C_F\otimes_{R_F}R_P\cong C_P$ for every later finite stage.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, last three paragraphs; corrected finite-normalization version (see report.md Source error).

proof.text: The limit rings have finite spectra: the structure lemma gives finitely many domain factors of dimension one and finitely many maximal ideals. After increasing $F_*$, contraction is bijective on ALL primes, for both $R_F\subseteq R_P$ and $C_F\subseteq C_P$. For every pair of distinct limit primes choose an element in their symmetric difference. Put these finitely many elements in a common finite stage by step 1. Their contractions are then distinct and remain distinct at later stages. Lying over [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] makes contraction surjective as well. Going up [pqf-lem-going-up] shows that its inverse preserves inclusion: lift an inclusion starting at its unique lower prime and use uniqueness of the upper lift. Thus these bijections identify maximal ideals and the primes contained in each maximal ideal. Write $q_F=q\cap C_F$, $n=q\cap R_P$, and $n_F=n\cap R_F$; then $n_F=q_F\cap R_F$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, last three paragraphs; corrected finite-normalization version (see report.md Source error).

proof.text: For each of the finitely many maximal ideals $n$ of $R_P$ choose a uniformizer $\pi_n\in(R_P)_n$. Express it as $a_n/s_n$ with $a_n,s_n\in R_P$ and $s_n\notin n$, and increase the finite stage to contain these numerators and denominators. Then $\pi_n$ belongs to $(R_F)_{n_F}$ and is a nonunit there. A nonunit in a DVR which generates the maximal ideal after a local embedding into another DVR already generates the source maximal ideal: writing the source maximal ideal as $(t)$, if $\pi_n=tu$ with $u$ a nonunit then its image lies in the square of the target maximal ideal, a contradiction. Apply this first to $(R_F)_{n_F}\to(R_P)_n$. For $q$ above $n$, the hypothesis $n(C_P)_q=q(C_P)_q$ says that the same $\pi_n$ is a uniformizer of $(C_P)_q$. Apply the same argument to $(C_F)_{q_F}\to(C_P)_q$. Therefore $\pi_n$ generates both finite-stage maximal ideals, giving $n_F(C_F)_{q_F}=q_F(C_F)_{q_F}$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, last three paragraphs; corrected finite-normalization version (see report.md Source error).

proof.text:
Fix $q_F$ and its unique lift $q$, and put $n=q\cap R_P$. Localize the canonical isomorphism of step 2 by $C_F\setminus q_F$. By the order-preserving spectrum bijection of step 3, the primes surviving in this localization of $C_P$ are exactly those contained in $q$. In particular there is just one maximal ideal, the one induced by $q$; all elements outside it are units. This localization is therefore $(C_P)_q$. Localizing the base by $R_P\setminus n$ then changes neither side, since these elements already become units. Hence
$$(C_F)_{q_F}\otimes_{(R_F)_{n_F}}(R_P)_n\cong(C_P)_q.$$
Quotient by $\pi_n$ and use step 4. The universal properties of the tensor product and quotient give the actual tensor-field isomorphism
$$\kappa(q_F)\otimes_{\kappa(n_F)}\kappa(n)\cong\kappa(q).$$
It is an isomorphism of $\kappa(n)$-algebras induced by residue maps, not merely equality of composita.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, last three paragraphs; corrected finite-normalization version (see report.md Source error).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-separability-tensor-field-descent] with $k=\kappa(n_F)$, $k'=\kappa(n)$ and $F=\kappa(q_F)$. The tensor product is a field by step 5 and is separable over $k'$ by its identification with the hypothesized separable extension $\kappa(q)/\kappa(n)$. Thus $\kappa(q_F)/\kappa(n_F)$ is separable. The stage is common to all finitely many limit maximal ideals; by step 3 these exhaust the finite-stage ones. Set $K_0=F$. Step 2 gives the local DVRs and maximal contractions, step 4 the equality of maximal ideals, and this step the remaining residue-separability conclusion.
